examples.derivation: The vertical scale doubles plotted heights. The tangent therefore passes through (0,2) and (6,8), giving gradient (8−2)/(6−0)=1. At x=3, the curve and tangent both have plotted height 2.5 and plotted gradient 0.5, confirming tangency and f'(3)≈1. This adapts the supplied graphical tangent exercises at lines 373–380.

Each horizontal square represents 4 minutes and each vertical square 10°C. The tangent intercepts are (0,50) and (20,0), so T'(8)≈(0−50)/(20−0)=−2.5°C/min. At plotted x=2, the exponential curve has height 3 and plotted gradient −1, matching the tangent at (8,30). The signed result and decreasing-temperature interpretation agree. This adapts the practical tangent-rate method at lines 385–415.
